---
title: "10 · Practice — Generating Functions"
---

Each solved exercise below isolates one modelling decision from the chapter:
sequence versus multiset, where the initial conditions live in a rational
function, and extracting a single Lagrange coefficient. They are small enough
to check by hand, which is the point — a wrong model is invisible in code.

## Solved exercises

### A. Sequences and multisets

Count objects of total size four whose parts have sizes one or two, first
when order matters and then when it does not.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Compare $1/(1-x-x^2)$ with $1/((1-x)(1-x^2))$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
Ordered sequences are 1111, 112, 121, 211, 22: five. Unordered objects are
1111, 112, 22: three. The first GF chooses a sequence of parts, while the
second independently chooses the multiplicity of each part size. Coefficients
through degree four are $(1,1,2,3,5)$ and $(1,1,2,2,3)$ respectively.
:::

### B. Recover initial conditions

Find the first four coefficients of $(2+x)/(1-x-x^2)$ and state the recurrence.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Compare coefficients in $(1-x-x^2)A=2+x$ before using the recurrence.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
$a_0=2$ and $a_1-a_0=1$, so $a_1=3$. For $n\ge2$,
$a_n=a_{n-1}+a_{n-2}$. The requested prefix is $2,3,5,8$.
For a huge $n$, use Bostan–Mori with this numerator and denominator; replacing
the numerator by the Fibonacci numerator would change the sequence.
:::

### C. Ordered forests

Let $T=x/(1-T)$ count nonempty plane rooted trees by vertices. Count ordered
pairs of such trees with a total of five vertices.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Use Lagrange with $n=5,k=2$, or convolve the small tree counts.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Solution"}
$[x^5]T^2=\frac25[t^3](1-t)^{-5}=\frac25\binom73=14$.
The independent check is $T=x+x^2+2x^3+5x^4+\cdots$, giving
$1\cdot5+1\cdot2+2\cdot1+5\cdot1=14$.
Modulo five the displayed division cannot be used directly; the integer
answer may be reduced afterward, or the convolution may be computed there.
:::

## 4. Codeforces 960G — Bandit Blues (`Mastery`)

- [Statement](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/960/G) ·
  [official tutorial](https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/58802) · English/Russian
- Train: permutation records, unsigned Stirling numbers, balanced polynomial products.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Condition on the position/value of the global maximum.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Left-to-right maxima and cycles of a permutation share the same Stirling distribution.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>For $A,B\ge1$, the answer simplifies to
$\binom{A+B-2}{A-1}\left[{N-1\atop A+B-2}\right]$.
Obtain the Stirling coefficient from the product $x(x+1)\cdots(x+N-2)$
using a balanced product tree. Handle $N=1$ with the empty product.</details>

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Why the simplification works"}
Cut at the global maximum. On each side, break the permutation at its records
(reading the right side backwards). Each record starts a block with its largest
element first; viewing the block cyclically is a permutation cycle. The remaining
$N-1$ labels therefore form $A+B-2$ cycles. Choose which $A-1$ cycles belong
on the left; record order reconstructs the two sides uniquely. This gives the
binomial factor and the first-kind Stirling coefficient. If either $A$ or $B$
is zero the answer is zero for a nonempty permutation.
:::
